Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

offer verb

to do something

also offer to help, offer one’s help, volunteer

classical

Caes. BG 4.21.5: quī polliceantur obsidēs dare
Plaut. Bacch. 185: hospitium et cēnam pollicēre

polliceor, pollicērī, pollicitus sum

verb, second conjugation, deponent · Conjugation on Wiktionary

offer, promise (to do something)

With a future infinitive (sē ventūrum pollicitus est), in comedy and in Caesar also a present; or with an object: operam pollicērī, to offer one’s help. The same verb serves for “promise”.

Other words

  • operam (suam) offerre — offer one’s help

    also used · classical · Liv. 40.23: in omnia ultrō suam offerēns operam (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • ā complūribus īnsulae cīvitātibus ad eum lēgātī veniunt, quī polliceantur obsidēs dare atque imperiō populī Rōmānī obtemperāre

    envoys come to him from several states of the island, to offer to give hostages and to submit to the rule of the Roman peopleCaes. BG 4.21.5

  • venīre tū mē gaudēs: ego crēdō tibi; hospitium et cēnam pollicēre, ut convenit peregrē advenientī

    You’re glad I’ve come: I believe you; you offer me a bed and dinner, as is right for someone arriving from abroadPlaut. Bacch. 184–186

  • Avus sē adjūtūrum pollicitus est.

    Grandpa offered to help.composed

See also offer, help.

SourcesLewis & Short: polliceor · Lewis & Short: offero · Lewis & Short: opera
